questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: The differences between men's and women's emotions
How zoos look after lizards, snakes and other reptiles
How gardeners can stop aphids from damaging plants
Animals that reproduce without males, and why sex exists
questions.why: They discuss female animals that don't need a male to make babies, and the 'paradox of sex'.

options: When males look after the eggs
When animals change from male to female
When a female reproduces without a mate
When two species mate together
questions.why: Neil says it's the process where the female can reproduce without a mate.

questions.q: What advantages of reproducing without sex does Rob mention?
options: They spread fast and need no mate
Their babies are bigger and stronger than others
They live longer
They need less food
questions.why: Rob says they can rapidly spread and control large areas and don't waste energy looking for a mate.

questions.q: According to Chris Wilson, what percentage of animal species are completely celibate?
options: About half
Less than one percent
About ten percent
Most of them
questions.why: He says less than one percent of all animal species are completely celibate.

questions.q: What does Chris Wilson call 'the paradox of sex'?
options: The fact that males are usually bigger than females
The fact that some animals mate only once in their lives
The fact that sex spreads diseases between many animals
Why sex is so common when going without it seems easier
questions.why: Despite the advantages of going without sex, few species do, which is a puzzle he calls the paradox of sex.

questions.q: How does Neil react to the idea that males might not be needed?
options: He is pleased and wants to know more
He jokes that he feels unappreciated
He doesn't believe it
He gets angry with Rob
questions.why: Neil says, 'As a male myself, I have to say I'm feeling a little underappreciated'.

questions.q: According to Amber Wright, how do American aphids reproduce?
options: Only by mating all through the year
Only females are ever born
All-female generations, then mating later
Males lay the eggs in spring
questions.why: She says they're all female for several generations, then at the end of summer males and females mate.

questions.q: Why is the aphids' strategy described as 'the best of both worlds'?
options: They clone to spread fast and use sex to mix their genes
They can live both on land and in water, like frogs
They eat both tomatoes and many other kinds of plants
They can live in both the US and Europe without problems
questions.why: Lucy Cooke says they use cloning to rapidly colonise and then sex to mix up the genes.
